title: MYP Individuals and Societies eAssessment Guide
summary: MYP Individuals and Societies eAssessment explained: understand the on-screen format, four criteria, task types, marking and final grades 1-7 step by step.
body_markdown:
The **MYP Individuals and Societies eAssessment** is a two-hour, externally marked, on-screen examination for MYP Year 5 students. It is not an ePortfolio subject. Students complete three broad tasks worth 80 marks in total, while the assessment addresses four equally weighted criteria: knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically.


That is the short answer. The more useful answer begins with what the examination feels like.


Imagine a hypothetical Year 5 student called Maya opening the exam. She knows historical examples, geographical processes, and relevant terminology. Yet the screen does not simply ask her to recite everything she remembers. It presents sources, contexts, arguments, and problems. Her real challenge is deciding which knowledge matters, how the evidence should be interpreted, and what kind of response the question requires.


That distinction explains most of the MYP Individuals and Societies exam. Knowledge gets you into the conversation. Judgment determines what you do once you are there.


### MYP eAssessment format at a glance


The IB currently identifies Individuals and Societies as an **on-screen examination** subject. The available disciplines include history, geography, and integrated humanities. This differs from MYP arts, design, and physical and health education, where external assessment is conducted through ePortfolios.


Feature What students should expect


Delivery On-screen examination


Duration Two hours


Total marks 80


Main structure Investigating, communicating, and thinking critically tasks


Criteria assessed A, B, C, and D


Marking External marking by trained IB examiners


Final result IB grade from 1-7


Students and parents can explore the dedicated[MYP Individuals and Societies subject resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-individuals-and-societies) for material aligned with this subject area. It is also worth reading the broader explanation of[which subjects use MYP eAssessment](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-subjects-have-myp-eassessment) , because the assessment method is not identical across every MYP subject.


A student questions an explorer emerging from a map about evidence while the explorer asks about the Wi-Fi


### The three tasks in the examination


The IB's published subject brief divides the 80 marks into three connected task types. These are not simply three content chapters. Each asks students to use knowledge in a different way.


### Investigating task


The investigating task is worth 26 marks and addresses criteria A and B. Students may evaluate an investigation, work with information supplied in the examination, and plan an investigation of their own.


Maya might therefore need to formulate or evaluate a research question, explain an appropriate method, identify useful evidence, or reflect on limitations. A response must be practical and specific. Saying that a researcher should "find reliable sources" is weaker than identifying suitable sources and explaining how they would help answer the research question.


### Communicating task


The communicating task is worth 18 marks and addresses criteria A and C. Students communicate ideas for a specified audience, purpose, and format.


The format matters. A speech, report, article, or other directed response should not sound identical. Students must select relevant knowledge, organize it clearly, and adopt a suitable style rather than pouring every remembered fact onto the screen.


### Thinking critically task


The thinking critically task is worth 36 marks and addresses criteria A, C, and D. It uses structured questions and culminates in extended writing about issues, evidence, arguments, or perspectives.


This is where source analysis becomes especially important. Strong answers do more than describe what a source says. They interpret its message, consider origin and purpose where relevant, examine value or limitations, connect evidence, and reach a supported judgment.


The[MYP Individuals and Societies eAssessment structure guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-individuals-societies-eassessment-structure) provides a useful companion explanation of these task demands.


### What the four assessment criteria mean


The four criteria organize what success looks like. Each has a maximum achievement level of 8 in school-based MYP assessment, producing a possible criterion total of 32. The on-screen examination instead awards marks across its tasks, with the blueprint designed so that all four criteria contribute equally overall.


Criterion What it assesses What a strong response does


A: Knowing and understanding Subject knowledge and conceptual understanding Uses accurate terminology, detailed knowledge, explanations, and relevant examples


B: Investigating Research questions, planning, methods, and reflection Designs a focused inquiry and justifies workable research choices


C: Communicating Organization, format, audience, purpose, and documentation Presents ideas clearly in the requested form and follows source instructions


D: Thinking critically Analysis, synthesis, evaluation, and perspectives Builds arguments, evaluates evidence, and reaches supported conclusions


Students often treat criterion A as the "content criterion" and everything else as technique. That separation is misleading. Knowledge appears across all three examination tasks. The difference is that students must make it useful.


For a deeper breakdown, read[the four Individuals and Societies criteria explained](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/myp-individuals-and-societies-criteria) . Students who are still mapping the curriculum can also review[topics covered in MYP Individuals and Societies](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-topics-are-covered-in-myp-individuals-and-societies) .


### How marks become grades 1-7


The final eAssessment result is reported on the IB scale from 1-7. It is important not to confuse this with adding four classroom criterion levels and applying a familiar school boundary table.


For the external examination, examiners award marks using the authorized markscheme. The assessment design gives equal weight to criteria A, B, C, and D, even though the three visible tasks carry different totals. The IB then applies grade boundaries to convert the examination outcome into a final subject grade from 1-7.


There is no responsible reason to memorize an unofficial universal raw-mark boundary. Boundaries can be determined for an examination session and should be checked through the school or official results documentation. A grade is therefore reached through this sequence:


1. The student completes the three on-screen tasks.
2. IB examiners award marks according to the markscheme.
3. Performance across the four criteria is equally weighted by the assessment design.
4. The relevant grade boundaries convert the result to a grade from 1-7.


A higher grade reflects stronger overall achievement across the assessed objectives, not merely the ability to recall more facts. The[guide to how MYP eAssessment grading works](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-does-myp-eassessment-work) explains the wider system, including the distinction between marks, boundaries, subject grades, and certificate requirements.


### How to prepare without revising blindly


Good preparation should resemble the decisions demanded by the examination.


Start with a content audit. Separate secure topics from genuine gaps, then use concise Study Notes and Flashcards to repair those gaps. RevisionDojo's[free Individuals and Societies resource guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-free-myp-individuals-and-societies-resources) can help students organize that process.


Next, move into application. A Questionbank is useful because it makes students retrieve knowledge inside a task rather than merely recognize it on a page. The[Individuals and Societies Questionbank guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-myp-individuals-and-societies-question-bank) explains how to choose practice by skill and topic.


After each response, ask three questions:


- Did I answer the command term?
- Did I use evidence rather than make unsupported claims?
- Did my organization suit the requested audience and format?


RevisionDojo brings Questionbank practice, Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, and AI-supported Grading tools into one study process. Its wider learning platform also includes Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, a Coursework Library, and Tutors where available for the relevant programme, subject, and plan. The point is not to use every tool every day. It is to select the tool that solves the problem currently limiting the response.


### A calm final checklist


Before the examination, students should be able to:


- explain all four criteria in their own words
- recognize investigating, communicating, and critical-thinking demands
- respond directly to command terms
- use sources as evidence rather than decoration
- compare perspectives and evaluate arguments
- write in the specified format for an audience and purpose
- plan time across a two-hour on-screen examination
- reserve a few minutes to review incomplete or unclear answers


The MYP Individuals and Societies eAssessment rewards something broader than memory. It rewards disciplined curiosity: knowing enough to notice what matters, then thinking carefully enough to explain why.


That is also where RevisionDojo becomes most valuable. It turns the examination from one intimidating two-hour event into a sequence of smaller, trainable skills. Learn the content, practise the decisions, review the evidence, and improve the next response.
